topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture's aims and its relationship to earlier teaching before the substantive discussion begins.

topics.label: Cellular changes driving cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how altered cellular states drive tumor development, extending the account of mutation-driven clonal selection to transformation through epigenetic disruption.

topics.label: Stemness, tumor hierarchy and the cell of origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how a cell's position in a tissue hierarchy and its capacity for self-renewal influence cancer initiation and propagation.

topics.label: Inflammation-induced stemness and cancer promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how inflammatory signals can confer stem-like properties that enable previously nonmalignant mutant cells to form tumors.

topics.label: Microenvironmental support of established tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines established tumors' dependence on supportive stromal cells and the therapeutic opportunities created by that dependence.

topics.label: Methods for investigating cancer evolution and cell interactions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how molecular profiling of human tissue can reveal tumor evolution and interactions within the tumor microenvironment.

topics.label: Multiple routes to malignancy through converging cellular and environmental conditions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic integrates the lecture's mechanisms into an account of the conditions permitting malignant outgrowth and extends that account to developmental timing and childhood cancer.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture and announces the forthcoming discussion of cancer therapy.
